title: How Do Birds Find Their Way?
context:
Every year, billions of birds travel thousands of kilometres between their breeding grounds and their winter homes, and many return to the very same tree or pond. How they find their way has fascinated scientists for centuries, and the answer, it turns out, is not a single instrument but a toolkit. Each tool has strengths and weaknesses, and birds appear to switch between them according to the weather, the time of day and the stage of the journey.

The first tool to be demonstrated was a sun compass. In the 1950s, a German researcher placed starlings in a circular cage with windows that let them see the sky but not the landscape. Whenever migration season came, the birds fluttered towards the same compass direction. When mirrors were used to shift the apparent position of the sun, the birds changed their direction by the same angle, proving that they were reading the sun. Since the sun moves across the sky during the day, the birds must also compensate for the time, which suggests that they possess an internal clock.

Many species travel at night, and for them the stars take over. In a classic experiment, young indigo buntings were raised inside a planetarium where the artificial sky could be controlled. The birds learned to find north by observing the point around which the stars appeared to rotate. Crucially, they did not memorise particular constellations: when the researchers made the sky rotate around a different star, the birds simply followed the new centre. Buntings that had never seen a night sky could not orient themselves at all, which shows that this ability must be learned early in life.

Birds also seem to sense the Earth's magnetic field. Robins kept in windowless rooms still hop in the direction they would normally migrate, and they become confused if the surrounding magnetic field is altered. How they detect it remains uncertain. One theory proposes that a light-sensitive protein in the eye allows birds to perceive the field as a pattern superimposed on their vision. Another suggested that tiny iron-rich particles in the beak act as a compass, but later studies found that similar particles were located in immune cells, not nerve cells, and enthusiasm for this idea has cooled.

A bird's methods change with experience. Young birds on their first journey appear to follow an inherited programme, flying in a particular direction for a particular length of time. In one study, researchers captured juvenile starlings during their autumn flight and released them hundreds of kilometres to the side. The young birds continued in the original direction and ended up in the wrong place, whereas adults corrected their course and reached their usual wintering area. Experienced birds apparently build up a mental map using landmarks such as coastlines and mountain ranges and, according to some studies, smell. Seabirds whose sense of smell was temporarily blocked often failed to find their way back to their colonies.

The overall picture, therefore, is of redundancy rather than perfection. Birds do not rely on one sense, but weigh several cues, and when these conflict, they can recalibrate: for example, migrating thrushes use the pattern of light at sunset to adjust their magnetic compass. This flexibility has a cost when people interfere. Bright city lights can attract night migrants away from their route and cause them to circle until exhausted, which is why some cities now switch off non-essential lighting during peak migration weeks.

questions.prompt: What point does the writer make in the first paragraph?
options: Bird navigation depends on a set of different abilities
Scientists have now fully explained how birds navigate
Most birds return to the same place each year by chance
Only a few species can travel long distances
questions.answer: Bird navigation depends on a set of different abilities
questions.why: Tác giả nói đáp án không phải một dụng cụ duy nhất mà là cả một bộ công cụ.
questions.quote: not a single instrument but a toolkit

questions.prompt: What did the experiment with mirrors show?
options: Starlings cannot navigate under cloudy skies
Birds prefer to travel towards the sun
Birds changed direction when the apparent position of the sun changed
Birds see better in a circular cage
questions.answer: Birds changed direction when the apparent position of the sun changed
questions.why: Khi gương dịch vị trí mặt trời, chim đổi hướng cùng góc, chứng tỏ chúng đọc mặt trời.
questions.quote: the birds changed their direction by the same angle

questions.prompt: Why must birds that use a sun compass have an internal clock?
options: To know when the migration season begins
To decide when to rest during the day
To tell the difference between the sun and the moon
To allow for the movement of the sun across the sky
questions.answer: To allow for the movement of the sun across the sky
questions.why: Mặt trời di chuyển trong ngày nên chim phải bù theo thời gian.
questions.quote: the birds must also compensate for the time

questions.prompt: In paragraph 3, 'orient themselves' means
options: recognise their parents
work out which way they should go
avoid other birds
remember the landscape
questions.answer: work out which way they should go
questions.why: 'Orient oneself' nghĩa là xác định phương hướng của mình.
questions.quote: could not orient themselves at all

questions.prompt: How did the indigo buntings learn to find north?
options: By memorising certain constellations
By following the brightest star
By observing the point around which the stars seem to turn
By comparing the moon with the stars
questions.answer: By observing the point around which the stars seem to turn
questions.why: Chim học tìm hướng bắc nhờ điểm mà các sao dường như quay quanh.
questions.quote: the point around which the stars appeared to rotate

questions.prompt: What happened when the researchers changed the centre of the artificial sky's rotation?
options: The birds followed the new centre
The birds became confused and stopped moving
The birds ignored the artificial sky
The birds returned to the original north
questions.answer: The birds followed the new centre
questions.why: Chim không nhớ chòm sao cụ thể mà đi theo tâm quay mới.
questions.quote: the birds simply followed the new centre

questions.prompt: What does the case of buntings that never saw a night sky show?
options: The ability is inherited from parents
The ability has to be learned early in life
The ability depends on the phase of the moon
The ability develops only after the first migration
questions.answer: The ability has to be learned early in life
questions.why: Chim chưa từng thấy bầu trời đêm không định hướng được, nên kỹ năng phải học từ nhỏ.
questions.quote: this ability must be learned early in life

questions.prompt: What suggests that robins can sense magnetic fields?
options: They avoid windowless rooms
They sing at different times of day
They fly faster in strong fields
They try to head in their migratory direction without seeing the sky
questions.answer: They try to head in their migratory direction without seeing the sky
questions.why: Chim cổ đỏ trong phòng không cửa sổ vẫn nhảy theo hướng di cư và rối khi từ trường bị đổi.
questions.quote: Robins kept in windowless rooms still hop in the direction they would normally migrate

questions.prompt: What is said about the theory involving a light-sensitive protein?
options: It has been disproved by later studies
It explains how birds find food
It proposes that birds see the field as a pattern in their vision
It applies only to night migrants
questions.answer: It proposes that birds see the field as a pattern in their vision
questions.why: Giả thuyết này cho rằng chim thấy từ trường như một hoạ tiết phủ lên thị giác. Bài không nói nó bị bác bỏ.
questions.quote: perceive the field as a pattern superimposed on their vision

questions.prompt: Why has enthusiasm for the theory about iron particles in the beak cooled?
options: The particles were too small to measure
Later studies found similar particles in immune cells, not nerve cells
Birds with damaged beaks could still navigate
Iron is not magnetic at body temperature
questions.answer: Later studies found similar particles in immune cells, not nerve cells
questions.why: Các hạt hoá ra nằm trong tế bào miễn dịch chứ không phải tế bào thần kinh.
questions.quote: similar particles were located in immune cells, not nerve cells

questions.prompt: What do young birds on their first journey appear to follow?
options: An inherited programme of direction and duration
The guidance of experienced adults
Landmarks along the coast
The smell of their home colony
questions.answer: An inherited programme of direction and duration
questions.why: Chim non theo chương trình di truyền: một hướng bay trong một khoảng thời gian.
questions.quote: an inherited programme, flying in a particular direction for a particular length of time

questions.prompt: What happened to the juvenile starlings that were moved sideways?
options: They flew back towards where they were captured
They stopped at the release site
They found their usual wintering area
They kept to the original direction and arrived in the wrong place
questions.answer: They kept to the original direction and arrived in the wrong place
questions.why: Chim non tiếp tục hướng cũ nên đến sai chỗ.
questions.quote: ended up in the wrong place

questions.prompt: How did the adult starlings behave differently from the juveniles?
options: They flew faster
They refused to fly
They corrected their course and reached the usual wintering area
They followed the juveniles
questions.answer: They corrected their course and reached the usual wintering area
questions.why: Chim trưởng thành điều chỉnh hướng và tới đúng nơi trú đông.
questions.quote: adults corrected their course and reached their usual wintering area

questions.prompt: In the last paragraph, 'redundancy' refers to
options: unnecessary waste of energy
the presence of more than one system for the same task
loss of ability with age
failure to complete a task
questions.answer: the presence of more than one system for the same task
questions.why: Dư thừa ở đây là nhiều tín hiệu/giác quan cùng làm một việc định hướng, đối lập với 'hoàn hảo'.
questions.quote: redundancy rather than perfection

questions.prompt: What do the experiments with seabirds suggest?
options: Smell may help experienced birds find their way home
Seabirds cannot use the sun
Seabirds rely on sight alone
Blocking their smell improves navigation
questions.answer: Smell may help experienced birds find their way home
questions.why: Chim biển bị bịt khứu giác thường không về được tổ.
questions.quote: often failed to find their way back to their colonies

questions.prompt: What do migrating thrushes do when cues conflict?
options: Ignore the magnetic field at sunset
Change their time of departure
Use the stars when the sunset is cloudy
Use the pattern of light at sunset to adjust their magnetic compass
questions.answer: Use the pattern of light at sunset to adjust their magnetic compass
questions.why: Ví dụ về hiệu chỉnh lại la bàn từ bằng mẫu ánh sáng lúc hoàng hôn.
questions.quote: use the pattern of light at sunset to adjust their magnetic compass

questions.prompt: Why does the writer say that flexibility 'has a cost'?
options: Birds use more energy when comparing cues
Flexible birds migrate less often
Human interference such as bright lights can mislead birds
Cues conflict more often in cities than in the countryside
questions.answer: Human interference such as bright lights can mislead birds
questions.why: Cái giá là chim dễ bị đánh lạc hướng bởi đèn đô thị.
questions.quote: This flexibility has a cost when people interfere.

questions.prompt: What can happen to night migrants near bright city lights?
options: They fly faster to escape
They may be drawn off their route and circle until exhausted
They stop migrating altogether
They lose their magnetic sense
questions.answer: They may be drawn off their route and circle until exhausted
questions.why: Đèn sáng thu hút chim đêm khỏi lộ trình và khiến chúng bay vòng đến kiệt sức.
questions.quote: cause them to circle until exhausted

questions.prompt: Why do some cities switch off non-essential lighting?
options: To protect migrating birds during peak weeks
To save electricity in summer
To make the stars more visible to residents
To reduce complaints from neighbours
questions.answer: To protect migrating birds during peak weeks
questions.why: Các thành phố tắt đèn không cần thiết trong tuần cao điểm di cư.
questions.quote: switch off non-essential lighting during peak migration weeks

questions.prompt: Which statement best summarises the passage?
options: A single sense is more reliable than a combination of cues
The sun compass is the most important tool
Navigation is mainly instinctive and cannot be learned
Birds navigate by combining several imperfect cues
questions.answer: Birds navigate by combining several imperfect cues
questions.why: Bài kết luận chim cân nhắc nhiều tín hiệu, linh hoạt hiệu chỉnh, chứ không dựa vào một giác quan.
questions.quote: Birds do not rely on one sense, but weigh several cues
